scope: Narrow owner-state correction, not widening existing fixture total deadline, creating alternate cleanup completion or asserting historical failures fixed.

limits: No actual fs.rm operation, per-directory completion, process-group absence or precise filesystem cause was observed in finalnative01.
FK-holder cleanup has only timeout/unconfirmed evidence; its exact cause is unknown.

installed_sdk_trace.fact: BrowserServer close and kill delegate directly to browser.options.browserProcess close and kill.
closeOrKill races gracefullyClose against its own SDK timer and on failure awaits kill. browserProcess exposes that close wrapper and original kill.
One waitForCleanup promise fulfills only from spawnedProcess close handler after cleanup().then(fulfillCleanup); child close and temporary-folder cleanup are separate events.

cleanup awaits removeFolders(tempDirectories), which awaits Promise.all of actual fs.promises.rm recursive force maxRetries10. Errors become values; cleanup logs them and still fulfills waitForCleanup. Promise fulfillment proves the attempt settled, not successful deletion of every folder.
gracefullyClose and killAndWait both await the same waitForCleanup. Repeating kill cannot create an independent completion path.

Default launch creates both artifacts and user-data directories under os.tmpdir, listing both in tempDirectories. Explicit artifactsDir remains caller-owned; default user-data directory stays SDK-owned.

proposed_state_transitions.behavior: Keep existing finalize-started 12000ms hard timer while awaiting the existing startup promise. No new tail clock.
Invoke actual browserServer.close once; retain its original observed promise and two-second request/completion observation. Mark close_settled only when that actual promise fulfills or rejects.

If close did not fulfill true within its two-second observation, invoke actual browserServer.kill once and retain its original observed promise. Keep existing two-second kill observation; rejection remains failure, never successful cleanup.

Only if the two-second kill observation expired pending AND actual child exit is established by exitCode/signalCode plus the observed child close event, await that same already-issued real kill promise under the still-running original 12000ms hard timer. Do not issue another close/kill, start another timeout or fabricate a settlement. If promise rejects/settles false or original hard timer expires, no ACK and exit3/unconfirmed outcome.

Require fulfilled true actual SDK cleanup and actual child exit before unchanged cleaned ACK, outcome, browser identity and Rust exit-code validation. Clearing original hard timer remains allowed only after confirmed ACK.

non_negotiable_preservation: Two-second close and two-second kill observations remain; additional time is only observation of already-issued real SDK artifact cleanup after actual child close, within the existing twelve-second total.
No SDK monkeypatch, shadowing, synthetic fulfillment, provider success, raw payload/path logging, process-only ACK, generic kill fallback or duplicate clock.
Existing catch/finally and unref retained hard bound on failed shutdown remain truthful.

Add typed private browser-cleanup stage in Rust CleanupStage together with Node stage metadata so new diagnostic is parseable. This needs a new exact Rust/source binding and focused fault candidate rebase, not an unnoticed schema drift.
Passing owned browser lifecycle probe does not certify credential ceremonies, business/browser scenario P16, complete native gate or launch.

SDK cleanup settlement is not complete temporary-file erasure evidence: upstream catches folder-removal errors and still fulfills. Owned-temp probes must independently observe residual folders and may not claim destruction from settlement alone.

empirical_owned_temp_probe_design.mechanism: Use a unique caller-created private TMPDIR for each actual resident child/probe. Supply through already allowed TMPDIR environment; pinned SDK remains unchanged. Capture only counts/classified existence of SDK default artifacts/user-data dirs and actual promise/event timing, never raw paths or bytes. Cleanup owner receives explicit custody of the unique temp root.
cases: Normal ready/done with actual Chromium identity and independent verified absence witness.
EOF after actual ready with the same custody and absence checks.
Verified owned Chromium process-group SIGSTOP then done, retaining actual SDK close/kill and independent absence.

A dedicated actual SDK launch/close observation may record child exit/close, close/kill promise settlement and owned-temp directory existence to localize removal delay; it must remain separate from native credential/business acceptance.
guards: No fs.rm interception or mutation of node_modules.
Never remove a directory or signal a process without verifying it belongs to this fresh instance; unavailable ownership remains UNKNOWN and fails custody acceptance.
A child exit flag does not establish descendant/group absence.
If delay does not reproduce, report NOT_REPRODUCED and keep exact directory cause UNPROVEN.
Use outer bounded harness custody; in-process timers cannot guarantee cleanup after SIGKILL/host failure.
Any raw private filesystem paths are transient internal references, excluded from report/log/telemetry.

required_reviews_and_proof: Independent design acceptance before Node implementation.
Exact source diff review covering both Node owner and Rust diagnostic tag, with no changed total/phase constants.
Real owned-temp lifecycle/dedicated SDK evidence; preserve unproven filesystem cause if no reproduction.
Focused startup-failure proof, unchanged short-family consumer and failing FK-holder consumer against final changed source.
Fresh full native/browser gate plus exact source maps; P16 diagnostic/fix remains separate.
